Standalone follow-up to Phase 1b of `survival.qmd`. Two questions:

1. Is each state's average net import/export rate actually stable from yearpair to yearpair, or is the average hiding sign switches, trends, or one-off spikes?
2. What do the Sankeys look like when built from each yearpair's own rate × that year's own stock, instead of from multi-year averages? And can gross imports and gross exports be matched more closely without rescaling anything?

Rates throughout use the production method, `old` (national-survival weights): net imports as a share of the state's own age 2-8 stock per year (negative = net export). In sections 1–3, counts are rate × that year's age 2-8 VIO stock (`value_stock` in `survival.qmd`). Section 4 adds age-mix accounting counts. Since 2026-10-14, `survival.qmd`'s production Sankeys use those counts, with the national-survival-weighted rate for their % labels.

**Inputs** (git-ignored, written by `survival.qmd`; copy them into `data/`):

- `net_imports_long.csv`, `state_vehtype_stock_by_year.csv`, `net_imports_summary.csv` (Phase 1b)
- `pipeline_state_survival_14to25.csv`, `pipeline_national_survival_14to25.csv` (Phase 1; only for the age-mix accounting section)

**Outputs:** `est net flows/by_year/` (git-ignored), Sankeys in its `sankey/` subfolder.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(geofacet)
library(networkD3)

data_dir   <- here::here("data")
out_dir    <- here::here("est net flows", "by_year")
sankey_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "sankey")
dir.create(sankey_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# FALSE skips re-drawing the ~80 Sankey HTML/PNG files (one headless-Chrome
# screenshot each) and reuses whatever PNGs are already on disk
render_sankeys <- TRUE

# saveWidget(selfcontained = TRUE) needs pandoc, which rmarkdown can't find
# outside RStudio unless pointed at RStudio's bundled copy
rstudio_pandoc <- "C:/Program Files/RStudio/resources/app/bin/quarto/bin/tools"
if (!nzchar(Sys.getenv("RSTUDIO_PANDOC")) && dir.exists(rstudio_pandoc)) {
  Sys.setenv(RSTUDIO_PANDOC = rstudio_pandoc)
}

# averaging windows, as in survival.qmd (start-year labels: 2014 = 2014/15)
year_sets <- list(
  yrs1519  = 2015:2019,
  yrs1421  = 2014:2021,
  yrs_excl = setdiff(2014:2024, c(2020, 2022)),
  yrs_all  = 2014:2024
)
year_set_labels <- c(
  yrs1519  = "2015/16–2019/20",
  yrs1421  = "2014/15–2021/22",
  yrs_excl = "2014/15–2024/25 excl. 20/21 & 22/23",
  yrs_all  = "2014/15–2024/25 (all)"
)
excl_years <- c(2020, 2022)   # yearpairs 2020/21 and 2022/23, dropped by yrs_excl
classes    <- c("Car", "SUV", "Pickup")

yp_label <- function(y) paste0(y, "/", str_sub(y + 1, 3, 4))
pct      <- function(x, acc = 1) scales::percent(x, accuracy = acc)

# chart chrome
col_ink   <- "#0b0b0b"
col_ink2  <- "#52514e"
col_muted <- "#898781"
col_grid  <- "#e1e0d9"
col_base  <- "#c3c2b7"
col_band  <- "#ecebe4"
col_exp   <- "#7b2d8e"   # exporter / importer colours match the Sankeys
col_imp   <- "#e67e22"
col_win   <- c(yrs_all = "#2a78d6", yrs_excl = "#eb6834")

theme_nb <- theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(color = col_grid, linewidth = 0.3),
        axis.text = element_text(color = col_ink2),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 12, color = col_ink),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(color = col_ink2),
        plot.caption = element_text(color = col_ink2, hjust = 0),
        strip.text = element_text(color = col_ink),
        legend.position = "top",
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#fcfcfb", color = NA))
```

```{r read-data}
stock <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "state_vehtype_stock_by_year.csv"),
                  show_col_types = FALSE)

rates <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "net_imports_long.csv"),
                  show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(method == "old") |>
  left_join(stock, by = join_by(year, statename, VehicleClass)) |>
  transmute(VehicleClass, statename,
            year = as.integer(year), yearpair = yp_label(year),
            rate = value, stock, count = value * stock, n_ages_used,
            excluded_from_yrs_excl = year %in% excl_years,
            # the workbook (and every window average) drops Tennessee's
            # first yearpair from the weighted-method averages
            tn_outlier = statename == "Tennessee" & year == 2014)

stopifnot(nrow(rates) == 3 * 51 * 11, !anyNA(rates$stock))

win_avg <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "net_imports_summary.csv"),
                    show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(method == "old") |>
  select(VehicleClass, statename, year_set, Average, Average_stock)

# the window averages are plain means of these per-year rates (TN 2014/15
# excluded), so the per-year view below is a decomposition of exactly the
# numbers the averaged Sankeys use
win_check <- imap(year_sets, \(yrs, nm) {
  rates |>
    filter(year %in% yrs, !tn_outlier) |>
    summarise(avg = mean(rate, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(VehicleClass, statename)) |>
    mutate(year_set = nm)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  inner_join(win_avg, by = join_by(VehicleClass, statename, year_set))
stopifnot(nrow(win_check) == 4 * 153, max(abs(win_check$avg - win_check$Average)) < 1e-12)

rates |>
  select(-n_ages_used) |>
  arrange(VehicleClass, statename, year) |>
  write_csv(file.path(out_dir, "netimports_rates_by_year_old.csv"))
```

# 1. Per-yearpair rates

Tidy table: `est net flows/by_year/netimports_rates_by_year_old.csv` (one row per class × state × yearpair: rate, stock, count, flags).

In the maps below each panel is one state. Reference lines are the all-years average (solid blue) and the `yrs_excl` average (dashed orange); shaded columns are 2020/21 and 2022/23, the two yearpairs `yrs_excl` drops. The y-axis is clipped at ±11% so the typical ±1–3% swings stay readable; anything beyond is drawn as a triangle at the edge with its real value printed beside it.

```{r rate-geofacets}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 11
ylim_rate <- c(-0.11, 0.11)

plot_geo_rates <- function(vc) {
  d <- rates |>
    filter(VehicleClass == vc) |>
    mutate(off_scale = case_when(rate > ylim_rate[2] ~ "above",
                                 rate < ylim_rate[1] ~ "below",
                                 .default = "within"),
           rate_plot = pmin(pmax(rate, ylim_rate[1]), ylim_rate[2]),
           in_excl   = if_else(excluded_from_yrs_excl,
                               "2020/21 or 2022/23 (dropped from yrs_excl)",
                               "other yearpairs"))

  refs <- win_avg |>
    filter(VehicleClass == vc, year_set %in% c("yrs_all", "yrs_excl")) |>
    mutate(window = factor(year_set, levels = c("yrs_all", "yrs_excl")))

  off <- filter(d, off_scale != "within")

  ggplot(d, aes(year, rate_plot)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = excl_years - 0.5, xmax = excl_years + 0.5,
             ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = col_band) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = col_base, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_hline(aes(yintercept = Average, color = window, linetype = window),
               data = refs, linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_line(color = col_ink2, linewidth = 0.4, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_point(aes(fill = in_excl), data = filter(d, off_scale == "within"),
               shape = 21, size = 1.3, stroke = 0.4, color = col_ink) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = off_scale), data = off, size = 1.8, color = col_ink) +
    # boxed so a label sitting over a neighbouring point/line stays legible
    geom_label(aes(label = pct(rate),
                   hjust = if_else(year >= 2022, 1.2, -0.2)),
               data = off, size = 2.2, color = col_ink, fill = "#fcfcfb",
               border.colour = NA, label.padding = unit(0.08, "lines")) +
    facet_geo(~ statename, grid = "us_state_grid2") +
    scale_color_manual(values = col_win, labels = year_set_labels[names(col_win)],
                       name = "Average over") +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(yrs_all = "solid", yrs_excl = "22"),
                          labels = year_set_labels[names(col_win)],
                          name = "Average over") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("2020/21 or 2022/23 (dropped from yrs_excl)" = "white",
                                 "other yearpairs" = col_ink),
                      name = NULL) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(above = 17, below = 25), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2014, 2019, 2024), labels = c("14/15", "19/20", "24/25")) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                       breaks = c(-0.05, 0, 0.05)) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = ylim_rate) +
    labs(title = paste0(vc, "s: net import rate by yearpair, each state (national-survival weights)"),
         subtitle = paste0("Share of the state's own age 2-8 stock per year; negative = net export. ",
                           "Shaded: 2020/21 and 2022/23. Tennessee 2014/15 is the known outlier the averages exclude."),
         x = "Yearpair", y = "Net import rate") +
    theme_nb +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7.5),
          axis.text = element_text(size = 6.5),
          panel.border = element_rect(color = col_grid, fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3))
}

for (vc in classes) {
  p <- plot_geo_rates(vc)
  ggsave(file.path(out_dir, paste0("rates_by_year_geofacet_", str_to_lower(vc), ".png")),
         plot = p, width = 16, height = 11, dpi = 150)
  print(p)
}
```

# 2. Is each state's average stable?

## Measures

Per state × class, over all 11 yearpairs (10 for Tennessee, whose 2014/15 is excluded as in the window averages; 10 for DC Pickup, whose 2016/17 is `NA`):

- **Spread:** SD and CV (SD / |mean|).
- **Single-yearpair spikes:** a yearpair at least 3.5 robust SDs (MAD) *and* at least 3 percentage points from the state's median. A spike matters for the average if dropping the spikes moves the all-years average by ≥ 0.5 pp, which is enough to change a whole-percent Sankey label.
- **Trend:** OLS slope of rate on year, fitted without spike yearpairs; p-values Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted within each class (153 tests would otherwise produce ~8 false positives at 5%). A trend counts if q < 0.05 and it moves the rate by ≥ 1 pp over the decade.
- **Role (importer/exporter) consistency:** share of yearpairs whose sign matches the sign of the spike-free average, and the number of sign flips between consecutive yearpairs.
- **Cross-state rank stability:** Spearman correlation across states between consecutive yearpairs, and between each yearpair and the average of all the other yearpairs.

**Verdict** (first rule that applies): *Spike-driven average* → *Trending* → *Role flips* (sign matches in < 80% of yearpairs) → *Stable importer / Stable exporter*. All flags that apply are listed in `flags`.

```{r stability-metrics}
spike_z  <- 3.5    # robust z (MAD units) from the state's median...
spike_pp <- 0.03   # ...and at least 3 pp away
shift_pp <- 0.005  # spikes move the all-years average by >= 0.5 pp
trend_pp <- 0.01   # trend moves the rate by >= 1 pp over 10 years
sign_min <- 0.8    # role holds in >= 80% of yearpairs

stab_input <- rates |>
  filter(!tn_outlier, !is.na(rate)) |>
  mutate(med   = median(rate),
         z     = (rate - med) / mad(rate),
         spike = abs(z) > spike_z & abs(rate - med) >= spike_pp,
         .by = c(VehicleClass, statename))

stability <- stab_input |>
  arrange(VehicleClass, statename, year) |>
  summarise(n_years       = n(),
            avg_all       = mean(rate),
            avg_excl      = mean(rate[!year %in% excl_years]),
            median        = median(rate),
            sd            = sd(rate),
            cv            = sd / abs(avg_all),
            n_spikes      = sum(spike),
            spike_years   = str_flatten(str_c(yearpair[spike], " (", pct(rate[spike]), ")"), ", "),
            avg_no_spikes = mean(rate[!spike]),
            spike_shift   = avg_all - avg_no_spikes,
            slope         = coef(lm(rate[!spike] ~ year[!spike]))[[2]],
            p_trend       = summary(lm(rate[!spike] ~ year[!spike]))$coefficients[2, 4],
            sign_share    = mean(sign(rate) == sign(avg_no_spikes)),
            role_flips    = sum(diff(sign(rate)) != 0),
            .by = c(VehicleClass, statename)) |>
  mutate(q_trend = p.adjust(p_trend, method = "BH"), .by = VehicleClass) |>
  mutate(role            = if_else(avg_no_spikes > 0, "importer", "exporter"),
         flag_spike      = abs(spike_shift) >= shift_pp,
         flag_trend      = q_trend < 0.05 & abs(slope * 10) >= trend_pp,
         flag_role       = sign_share < sign_min,
         flags = pmap_chr(list(flag_spike, flag_trend, flag_role), \(s, t, r) {
           str_flatten(c("spike", "trend", "role flips")[c(s, t, r)], ", ")
         }),
         verdict = case_when(flag_spike ~ "Spike-driven average",
                             flag_trend ~ "Trending",
                             flag_role  ~ "Role flips",
                             .default   = paste("Stable", role)),
         verdict_group = if_else(str_starts(verdict, "Stable"), "Stable", verdict))

# the all-years / yrs_excl columns reproduce net_imports_summary exactly
avg_check <- stability |>
  inner_join(win_avg |>
               filter(year_set %in% c("yrs_all", "yrs_excl")) |>
               select(-Average_stock) |>
               pivot_wider(names_from = year_set, values_from = Average),
             by = join_by(VehicleClass, statename))
stopifnot(nrow(avg_check) == 153,
          max(abs(avg_check$avg_all - avg_check$yrs_all)) < 1e-12,
          max(abs(avg_check$avg_excl - avg_check$yrs_excl)) < 1e-12)

stability |>
  select(VehicleClass, statename, verdict, flags, role, n_years,
         avg_all, avg_excl, avg_no_spikes, median, sd, cv,
         n_spikes, spike_years, spike_shift,
         slope_per_yr = slope, p_trend, q_trend, sign_share, role_flips) |>
  arrange(VehicleClass, verdict, statename) |>
  write_csv(file.path(out_dir, "netimports_stability_by_state_old.csv"))
```

```{r stability-summary-table}
verdict_levels <- c("Stable importer", "Stable exporter", "Role flips",
                    "Trending", "Spike-driven average")

stability |>
  count(VehicleClass, verdict) |>
  mutate(verdict = factor(verdict, levels = verdict_levels),
         VehicleClass = factor(VehicleClass, levels = classes)) |>
  arrange(verdict) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = VehicleClass, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  select(verdict, all_of(classes)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "States per verdict (of 51), national-survival weights, all 11 yearpairs")
```

```{r unstable-table}
stability |>
  filter(!str_starts(verdict, "Stable")) |>
  mutate(VehicleClass = factor(VehicleClass, levels = classes),
         verdict = factor(verdict, levels = verdict_levels)) |>
  arrange(verdict, VehicleClass, statename) |>
  transmute(Verdict = verdict, Class = VehicleClass, State = statename,
            `Avg all` = pct(avg_all, 0.1), `Avg excl` = pct(avg_excl, 0.1),
            `Avg w/o spikes` = pct(avg_no_spikes, 0.1),
            SD = pct(sd, 0.1),
            `Trend (pp/10 yr)` = sprintf("%+.1f", slope * 1000),
            `q trend` = signif(q_trend, 2),
            `Sign share` = pct(sign_share),
            Spikes = spike_years) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "States whose average is not stable, with the reason")
```

## Heatmap of every state × yearpair

Rows are ordered by the all-years average; the two right-hand columns are the `yrs_all` and `yrs_excl` averages. Cells are clipped at ±6% for colour (spikes go well beyond); × marks a spike yearpair, and the dot after the state name gives its verdict.

```{r heatmap}
#| fig-width: 15
#| fig-height: 12
heat_lim <- 0.06

heat_years <- rates |>
  left_join(select(stab_input, VehicleClass, statename, year, spike),
            by = join_by(VehicleClass, statename, year)) |>
  transmute(VehicleClass, statename, column = yearpair, rate,
            spike = coalesce(spike, FALSE), tn_outlier)

heat_avgs <- win_avg |>
  filter(year_set %in% c("yrs_all", "yrs_excl")) |>
  transmute(VehicleClass, statename,
            column = if_else(year_set == "yrs_all", "avg all", "avg excl"),
            rate = Average, spike = FALSE, tn_outlier = FALSE)

col_levels <- c(yp_label(2014:2024), "avg all", "avg excl")

# one row per state within each class facet, ordered by the all-years average
heat <- bind_rows(heat_years, heat_avgs) |>
  left_join(select(stability, VehicleClass, statename, avg_all, verdict_group),
            by = join_by(VehicleClass, statename)) |>
  mutate(VehicleClass = factor(VehicleClass, levels = classes),
         column = factor(column, levels = col_levels),
         row = fct_reorder(paste0(statename, "___", VehicleClass), avg_all),
         # marks on dark (clipped / near-clipped) cells need light ink
         mark_col = if_else(abs(rate) > 0.035, "white", col_ink))

verdict_cols <- c("Stable" = "#e1e0d9", "Role flips" = "#1baf7a",
                  "Trending" = "#eb6834", "Spike-driven average" = "#2a78d6")

p_heat <- ggplot(heat, aes(column, row)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = pmin(pmax(rate, -heat_lim), heat_lim)),
            color = "white", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_text(aes(label = "×", color = I(mark_col)), data = filter(heat, spike), size = 2.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = "TN", color = I(mark_col)), data = filter(heat, tn_outlier), size = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(x = 0.2, color = verdict_group),
             data = distinct(heat, VehicleClass, row, verdict_group), size = 1.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 11.5, color = col_ink2, linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(vars(VehicleClass), scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) str_remove(x, "___.*$")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = \(x) if_else(x %in% yp_label(excl_years), paste0(x, "*"), x)) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#c8312f", mid = "#f0efec", high = "#1c5cab",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-heat_lim, heat_lim),
                       labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                       name = "Net import rate") +
  scale_color_manual(values = verdict_cols, breaks = names(verdict_cols), name = "Verdict") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.2, 13.5), clip = "off") +
  labs(title = "Net import rate by state and yearpair (national-survival weights)",
       subtitle = "Blue = net importer, red = net exporter. * = dropped from yrs_excl. × = single-yearpair spike. Colour clipped at ±6%. Grey = NA (DC Pickup 2016/17).",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_nb +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 7),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6.5),
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        legend.box = "horizontal")

ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "rates_heatmap_all_classes.png"),
       plot = p_heat, width = 15, height = 12, dpi = 150)
p_heat
```

## Cross-state rank stability

```{r rank-stability}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.5
xs <- rates |> filter(!tn_outlier, !is.na(rate))

rank_cor <- map(2014:2024, \(y) {
  this <- xs |> filter(year == y) |> select(VehicleClass, statename, rate)
  prev <- xs |> filter(year == y - 1) |> select(VehicleClass, statename, prev = rate)
  loo  <- xs |> filter(year != y) |>
    summarise(loo = mean(rate), .by = c(VehicleClass, statename))
  this |>
    left_join(prev, by = join_by(VehicleClass, statename)) |>
    left_join(loo, by = join_by(VehicleClass, statename)) |>
    summarise(`vs previous yearpair` = if (all(is.na(prev))) NA_real_ else
                cor(rate, prev, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
              `vs average of the other yearpairs` = cor(rate, loo, method = "spearman"),
              cross_state_sd = sd(rate),
              .by = VehicleClass) |>
    mutate(year = y)
}) |>
  list_rbind()

rank_cor |>
  mutate(yearpair = yp_label(year)) |>
  write_csv(file.path(out_dir, "rank_correlation_by_yearpair.csv"))

# share of the state-year variance that is persistent between-state
# differences (vs year-to-year movement within a state)
var_share <- bind_rows(
  `all yearpairs`  = xs,
  `spikes removed` = semi_join(xs, filter(stab_input, !spike),
                               by = join_by(VehicleClass, statename, year)),
  .id = "sample") |>
  summarise(state_mean = mean(rate), within_var = var(rate),
            .by = c(sample, VehicleClass, statename)) |>
  summarise(between_share = var(state_mean) / (var(state_mean) + mean(within_var)),
            .by = c(sample, VehicleClass))

p_rank <- rank_cor |>
  select(-cross_state_sd) |>
  pivot_longer(starts_with("vs"), names_to = "comparison", values_to = "rho") |>
  filter(!is.na(rho)) |>
  mutate(VehicleClass = factor(VehicleClass, levels = classes)) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, rho, color = comparison)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = excl_years - 0.5, xmax = excl_years + 0.5,
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = col_band) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  facet_wrap(vars(VehicleClass)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`vs previous yearpair` = "#2a78d6",
                                `vs average of the other yearpairs` = "#eb6834"),
                     name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2014, 2017, 2020, 2023), labels = yp_label) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.4, 1)) +
  labs(title = "How well does one yearpair's state ranking match the others?",
       subtitle = "Spearman correlation across 51 states (TN 2014/15 excluded). Shaded: 2020/21 and 2022/23.",
       x = "Yearpair", y = "Spearman rho") +
  theme_nb

ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "rank_correlation_by_yearpair.png"),
       plot = p_rank, width = 10, height = 4.5, dpi = 150)
p_rank

var_share |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = between_share) |>
  mutate(across(-VehicleClass, \(x) pct(x))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Share of state-yearpair variance that is persistent between-state difference")

rank_cor |>
  transmute(VehicleClass, yearpair = yp_label(year), sd = pct(cross_state_sd, 0.1)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = VehicleClass, values_from = sd) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Cross-state SD of the net import rate, by yearpair")
```

## Verdict map

```{r verdict-map}
#| fig-width: 15
#| fig-height: 5
grid <- geofacet::us_state_grid2

p_vmap <- stability |>
  left_join(grid, by = join_by(statename == name)) |>
  mutate(VehicleClass = factor(VehicleClass, levels = classes),
         label = paste0(code, "\n", sprintf("%+.1f", 100 * avg_all))) |>
  ggplot(aes(col, -row)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = verdict_group), color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 2.3, lineheight = 0.85, color = col_ink) +
  facet_wrap(vars(VehicleClass), nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = verdict_cols, breaks = names(verdict_cols), name = NULL) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "Is the state's average net import rate stable? (national-survival weights, 11 yearpairs)",
       subtitle = "Label: state and all-years average rate (%). Verdict rules in the text above.") +
  theme_void(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        plot.title = element_text(size = 12, color = col_ink),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(color = col_ink2),
        strip.text = element_text(color = col_ink, size = 11),
        plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#fcfcfb", color = NA))

ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "stability_verdict_map.png"),
       plot = p_vmap, width = 15, height = 5, dpi = 150)
p_vmap
```

# 3. Per-yearpair Sankeys

Same layout as `make_sankey` in `survival.qmd` (top 15 exporters and importers, the rest lumped; widths are the real, unscaled counts; the gross-imports-to-exports gap is stated in the caption). Changes: an optional extra caption line naming single-yearpair spikes so they are not mistaken for migration; wider node padding (19 vs 13) so the labels of the thinnest exporter nodes don't overlap; and the title/caption capped at 860px so long titles aren't cut off at the PNG's right edge.

Files: `est net flows/by_year/sankey/sankey_net_flow_<class>_old_<yearpair>.png` (+ `.html`), plus the `yrs_all` and `yrs_excl` averages re-drawn alongside as `..._avg_<window>.png`.

```{r sankey-helpers}
method_label <- "national-survival weights"

# df: one row per state, columns STNAME + flow (net imports, vehicles/yr)
# + rate (net imports as a share of the state's own stock, per yr)
make_sankey <- function(df, title_text, extra_note = NULL) {
  exporters <- df |>
    filter(flow < 0) |>
    mutate(flow = abs(flow)) |>
    arrange(desc(flow))

  importers <- df |>
    filter(flow > 0) |>
    arrange(desc(flow))

  # top 15 + other
  if (nrow(exporters) > 15) {
    exporters <- bind_rows(
      slice_head(exporters, n = 15),
      tibble(STNAME = "Other exporters",
             flow = sum(exporters$flow[16:nrow(exporters)]),
             rate = NA_real_)
    )
  }
  if (nrow(importers) > 15) {
    importers <- bind_rows(
      slice_head(importers, n = 15),
      tibble(STNAME = "Other importers",
             flow = sum(importers$flow[16:nrow(importers)]),
             rate = NA_real_)
    )
  }

  # gross imports as a share of gross exports across states
  # (top-15 lumping preserves sums)
  actual_balance <- sum(importers$flow) / sum(exporters$flow)

  # link widths are the real, unscaled flows; the gap between gross exports
  # and gross imports is reported in the caption, never rescaled away.
  # "State (count; rate)" with the rate to the nearest whole percent; the
  # lumped "Other" nodes pool states with different rates, so count only
  node_labels <- function(d) {
    rate_txt <- if_else(is.na(d$rate), "",
                        paste0("; ", scales::percent(d$rate, accuracy = 1)))
    paste0(d$STNAME, " (", scales::comma(round(d$flow, -2)), rate_txt, ")")
  }
  exp_labels <- node_labels(exporters)
  imp_labels <- node_labels(importers)
  pool_label <- "Net flow pool"

  nodes <- tibble(
    name  = c(exp_labels, pool_label, imp_labels),
    group = c(rep("exporter", nrow(exporters)), "pool", rep("importer", nrow(importers)))
  ) |>
    mutate(id = row_number() - 1L)

  pool_id <- nodes |> filter(group == "pool") |> pull(id)

  links <- bind_rows(
    tibble(source = match(exp_labels, nodes$name) - 1L,
           target = pool_id,
           value  = exporters$flow),
    tibble(source = pool_id,
           target = match(imp_labels, nodes$name) - 1L,
           value  = importers$flow)
  )

  color_js <- 'd3.scaleOrdinal().domain(["exporter","pool","importer"]).range(["#7b2d8e","#aaaaaa","#e67e22"])'

  # nodePadding 19 (survival.qmd: 13) keeps the 18px labels of the thinnest
  # nodes (bottom of the exporter column) from overlapping each other
  s <- sankeyNetwork(
    Links = as.data.frame(links), Nodes = as.data.frame(nodes),
    Source = "source", Target = "target", Value = "value",
    NodeID = "name", NodeGroup = "group", colourScale = color_js,
    fontSize = 18, fontFamily = "sans-serif",
    nodeWidth = 20, nodePadding = 19, sinksRight = TRUE,
    width = 900, height = 900
  )

  balance_note <- paste0(
    "Gross imports = ", scales::percent(actual_balance, accuracy = 0.1),
    " of gross exports across states. ",
    "Labels: vehicles/yr; % of the state's own age 2-8 stock per year.")

  # the widget page is wider than the 920px screenshot, so cap the text width
  # or long titles get cut off at the right edge of the PNG
  text_style <- "max-width:860px; text-align:center; font-family:sans-serif;"
  htmlwidgets::prependContent(
    s,
    htmltools::tags$h3(title_text, style = text_style),
    htmltools::tags$p(balance_note, style = paste(text_style, "color:#555555;")),
    if (!is.null(extra_note))
      htmltools::tags$p(extra_note, style = paste(text_style, "color:#555555; margin-top:-8px;"))
  )
}

save_sankey <- function(s, stem) {
  html_file <- file.path(sankey_dir, paste0(stem, ".html"))
  png_file  <- file.path(sankey_dir, paste0(stem, ".png"))
  htmlwidgets::saveWidget(s, file = html_file, selfcontained = TRUE)
  webshot2::webshot(html_file, file = png_file, vwidth = 920, vheight = 1040, delay = 1)
  invisible(png_file)
}

sankey_stem <- function(vc, period, variant = "old") {
  paste0("sankey_net_flow_", str_to_lower(vc), "_", variant, "_",
         str_replace(period, "/", "-"))
}

# caption line naming that yearpair's spikes (and the TN outlier) for one class
spike_note <- function(vc, y) {
  sp <- stab_input |>
    filter(VehicleClass == vc, year == y, spike) |>
    arrange(desc(abs(rate)))
  parts <- c(
    if (y == 2014) "Tennessee 2014/15 is the known outlier the window averages exclude",
    if (nrow(sp) > 0) paste0("Single-yearpair spikes (state's usual rate in brackets): ",
                             str_flatten(paste0(sp$statename, " ", pct(sp$rate),
                                                " (", pct(sp$med), ")"), ", "))
  )
  if (length(parts) == 0) NULL else paste0(str_flatten(parts, ". "), ".")
}
```

```{r sankey-per-year}
#| results: hide
# basis names how the counts and % were made (the age-mix Sankeys don't
# use national-survival weights for their counts, so it isn't a fixed label)
sankey_title <- function(vc, when, basis) {
  paste0("Net Export and Import of ", vc, "s per year, ", when,
         " (age 2-8 vehicles; ", basis, "). ",
         "Includes vehicle movements associated with both population migration and vehicle markets.")
}

if (render_sankeys) {
  for (vc in classes) {
    for (y in 2014:2024) {
      df <- rates |>
        filter(VehicleClass == vc, year == y, !is.na(count)) |>
        select(STNAME = statename, flow = count, rate)
      s <- make_sankey(df,
                       sankey_title(vc, paste("yearpair", yp_label(y)),
                                    paste0(method_label, "; that yearpair's rate × that year's stock")),
                       extra_note = spike_note(vc, y))
      save_sankey(s, sankey_stem(vc, yp_label(y)))
    }
    for (ys in c("yrs_all", "yrs_excl")) {
      df <- win_avg |>
        filter(year_set == ys, VehicleClass == vc, !is.na(Average_stock)) |>
        select(STNAME = statename, flow = Average_stock, rate = Average)
      s <- make_sankey(df, sankey_title(vc, paste("averaged over", year_set_labels[ys]),
                                        paste0(method_label, "; mean of the per-yearpair counts")))
      save_sankey(s, sankey_stem(vc, paste0("avg_", ys)))
    }
  }
}
```

## How much do the top exporters and importers change?

```{r top15-membership}
#| fig-width: 15
#| fig-height: 12
period_flows <- bind_rows(
  rates |>
    filter(!is.na(count)) |>
    transmute(VehicleClass, statename, period = yearpair, flow = count),
  win_avg |>
    filter(year_set %in% c("yrs_all", "yrs_excl")) |>
    transmute(VehicleClass, statename,
              period = if_else(year_set == "yrs_all", "avg all", "avg excl"),
              flow = Average_stock)
)

top15 <- period_flows |>
  mutate(exp_rank = rank(if_else(flow < 0, flow, NA), na.last = "keep", ties.method = "min"),
         imp_rank = rank(if_else(flow > 0, -flow, NA), na.last = "keep", ties.method = "min"),
         rank = coalesce(exp_rank, imp_rank),
         role = case_when(exp_rank <= 15 ~ "Top-15 exporter",
                          flow < 0       ~ "Other exporter",
                          imp_rank <= 15 ~ "Top-15 importer",
                          .default       = "Other importer"),
         .by = c(VehicleClass, period))

# top-k exporter / importer sets for every class x period
top_sets <- function(k) {
  top15 |>
    summarise(exp = list(statename[!is.na(exp_rank) & exp_rank <= k]),
              imp = list(statename[!is.na(imp_rank) & imp_rank <= k]),
              .by = c(VehicleClass, period))
}

# how many of each yearpair's top-k are also top-k in the reference: the
# yrs_excl averaged Sankey, or the previous yearpair's Sankey
overlap_counts <- function(k) {
  sets <- top_sets(k) |> filter(period %in% yp_label(2014:2024))
  vs_avg <- top_sets(k) |>
    filter(period == "avg excl") |>
    select(VehicleClass, ref_exp = exp, ref_imp = imp)
  vs_prev <- sets |>
    mutate(period = yp_label(as.integer(str_sub(period, 1, 4)) + 1)) |>
    select(VehicleClass, period, ref_exp = exp, ref_imp = imp)
  bind_rows(
    `yrs_excl average`   = left_join(sets, vs_avg, by = join_by(VehicleClass)),
    `previous yearpair`  = inner_join(sets, vs_prev, by = join_by(VehicleClass, period)),
    .id = "reference") |>
    transmute(reference, VehicleClass, period, k = k,
              exporters = map2_int(exp, ref_exp, \(a, b) length(intersect(a, b))),
              importers = map2_int(imp, ref_imp, \(a, b) length(intersect(a, b))))
}

overlap <- bind_rows(overlap_counts(15), overlap_counts(5))

overlap |> write_csv(file.path(out_dir, "top_k_overlap_by_yearpair.csv"))

overlap |>
  pivot_longer(c(exporters, importers), names_to = "side", values_to = "in_common") |>
  summarise(median = median(in_common), min = min(in_common),
            worst = str_flatten(period[in_common == min(in_common)], ", "),
            .by = c(reference, k, VehicleClass, side)) |>
  mutate(VehicleClass = factor(VehicleClass, levels = classes)) |>
  arrange(desc(reference), desc(k), VehicleClass, side) |>
  transmute(`Compared with` = reference, `Top k` = k, Class = VehicleClass, Side = side,
            `Median in common` = paste0(median, " of ", k),
            `Fewest in common` = paste0(min, " of ", k), `In yearpair(s)` = worst) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "How many of each yearpair's top-k states are also top-k in the comparison Sankey")

role_cols <- c("Top-15 exporter" = col_exp, "Other exporter" = "#d9c2df",
               "Top-15 importer" = col_imp, "Other importer" = "#f6d5b5")

top15_plot <- top15 |>
  left_join(filter(win_avg, year_set == "yrs_excl") |> select(VehicleClass, statename, ref = Average_stock),
            by = join_by(VehicleClass, statename)) |>
  mutate(VehicleClass = factor(VehicleClass, levels = classes),
         period = factor(period, levels = col_levels),
         row = fct_reorder(paste0(statename, "___", VehicleClass), ref),
         role = factor(role, levels = names(role_cols)))

p_top <- ggplot(top15_plot, aes(period, row, fill = role)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = role_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Who makes the Sankey's top 15, yearpair by yearpair?",
       subtitle = "Number = rank by count within exporters / importers. Rows ordered by the yrs_excl average count. * = dropped from yrs_excl.",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_nb +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 7),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6.5),
        panel.grid.major = element_blank())

ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "top15_membership_by_yearpair.png"),
       plot = p_top, width = 15, height = 12, dpi = 150)
```

# 4. Matching gross imports and gross exports: age-mix accounting

## Where the gap comes from

The production count for state *s* is its rate times its whole age 2-8 stock:

count~s~ = stock~s~ × Σ~a~ w̃~a~ d~s,a~,

where d~s,a~ is the state-minus-national survival difference at age *a* and w̃~a~ are the normalised national cumulative-survival weights (a synthetic, stationary national age mix, the same for every state).

National survival at each age is the pooled ratio over the 51 states (checked below), so for every age the stock-weighted survival differences cancel exactly: Σ~s~ n~s,a~ d~s,a~ = 0, where n~s,a~ is the state's actual stock at age *a* in year *t*. The production counts don't cancel because they weight each state's d~s,a~ by stock~s~ × w̃~a~ instead of by n~s,a~. The national gap therefore splits exactly into two parts:

- **national age mix vs. synthetic weights:** Σ~a~ (w̃~a~ − p~a~) Σ~s~ stock~s~ d~s,a~, with p~a~ the actual national age mix;
- **state age mix vs. national age mix:** Σ~s~ stock~s~ Σ~a~ (p~a~ − p~s,a~) d~s,a~, with p~s,a~ the state's own age mix.

## The alternative: count survivors against national survival, age by age

count~s~ = Σ~a~ n~s,a~ d~s,a~ = Σ~a~ [observed survivors~s,a~ − national survival~a~ × n~s,a~]

This is the number of age 2-8 vehicles the state has in year *t*+1 beyond what national survival would leave it, which is the literal survival-residual definition of net migration. Its rate (count ÷ stock) is the state's survival differences weighted by its *own* observed age mix instead of the synthetic national one. Gross imports equal gross exports by construction in every yearpair; nothing is rescaled.

Since 2026-10-14, `survival.qmd`'s production Sankeys use these counts for their vehicle numbers and ribbon widths (`Average_agemix`). The % labels, maps and the stability analysis above keep the national-survival-weighted rate, which is age-standardized and so comparable across states regardless of fleet age. The age-mix Sankeys below are drawn the same way, so their % labels match the production ones.

```{r agemix-accounting}
age_counts <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "pipeline_state_survival_14to25.csv"),
                       show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(Age1 >= 2, Age1 <= 8) |>
  transmute(year = as.integer(str_sub(as.character(year_pair), 1, 4)),
            statename = state_name, VehicleClass, age = Age1,
            n_t = CY1, n_t1 = CY2)

nat_counts <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "pipeline_national_survival_14to25.csv"),
                       show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(Age1 >= 2, Age1 <= 8) |>
  transmute(year = as.integer(str_sub(as.character(year_pair), 1, 4)),
            VehicleClass, age = Age1, N_t = CY1, N_t1 = CY2)

# national survival is exactly the pooled ratio of the 51 states
pooled <- age_counts |>
  summarise(s_t = sum(n_t), s_t1 = sum(n_t1), .by = c(year, VehicleClass, age)) |>
  inner_join(nat_counts, by = join_by(year, VehicleClass, age))
stopifnot(nrow(pooled) == 11 * 3 * 7, all(pooled$s_t == pooled$N_t), all(pooled$s_t1 == pooled$N_t1))

nat_age <- nat_counts |>
  arrange(VehicleClass, year, age) |>
  mutate(S_nat = N_t1 / N_t,
         w     = cumprod(S_nat),
         w_n   = w / sum(w),           # production's synthetic age weights
         p_nat = N_t / sum(N_t),       # actual national age mix
         .by = c(VehicleClass, year))

ages <- age_counts |>
  left_join(nat_age, by = join_by(year, VehicleClass, age)) |>
  mutate(d       = n_t1 / n_t - S_nat,
         stock_s = sum(n_t),
         p_s     = n_t / stock_s,
         .by = c(year, statename, VehicleClass))

agemix <- ages |>
  summarise(rate_rebuilt  = sum(w_n * d),
            count_agemix  = sum(n_t1 - S_nat * n_t),
            stock_s       = first(stock_s),
            .by = c(VehicleClass, statename, year)) |>
  mutate(rate_agemix = count_agemix / stock_s) |>
  left_join(select(rates, VehicleClass, statename, year, yearpair, rate, count, stock, tn_outlier),
            by = join_by(VehicleClass, statename, year))

# the production rates rebuild exactly from the age-level counts (DC Pickup
# 2016/17 is NA in production because one age's survival is >= 2 and gets
# trimmed; the counts themselves are fine, so the age-mix version keeps it)
rebuilt <- agemix |> filter(!is.na(rate))
stopifnot(max(abs(rebuilt$rate_rebuilt - rebuilt$rate)) < 1e-12,
          all(agemix$stock_s == agemix$stock))

# and the age-mix counts sum to zero nationally in every class x yearpair
agemix_net <- agemix |> summarise(net = sum(count_agemix), .by = c(VehicleClass, year))
stopifnot(max(abs(agemix_net$net)) < 1e-3)

# exact decomposition of the production gap
gap_decomp <- ages |>
  mutate(D = sum(stock_s * d), .by = c(VehicleClass, year, age)) |>
  summarise(gap_total   = sum(stock_s * w_n * d),
            gap_natmix  = sum((w_n - p_nat) * stock_s * d),
            gap_statemix = sum(stock_s * (p_nat - p_s) * d),
            .by = c(VehicleClass, year)) |>
  left_join(select(balance_year, VehicleClass, year, gross_exports),
            by = join_by(VehicleClass, year))
stopifnot(max(abs(gap_decomp$gap_total - gap_decomp$gap_natmix - gap_decomp$gap_statemix)) < 1e-6)

agemix |>
  transmute(VehicleClass, statename, year, yearpair, stock,
            rate_production = rate, count_production = count,
            rate_agemix, count_agemix, tn_outlier) |>
  arrange(VehicleClass, statename, year) |>
  write_csv(file.path(out_dir, "netimports_by_year_production_vs_agemix.csv"))

gap_decomp |>
  mutate(VehicleClass = factor(VehicleClass, levels = classes)) |>
  arrange(VehicleClass, year) |>
  transmute(Class = VehicleClass, Yearpair = yp_label(year),
            `Production gap (veh/yr)` = scales::comma(round(gap_total, -2)),
            `Gap / gross exports` = pct(gap_total / gross_exports, 0.1),
            `from national age mix` = pct(gap_natmix / gap_total),
            `from state age mixes` = pct(gap_statemix / gap_total)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Production net national imbalance (gross imports − gross exports) and its exact split. Shares can exceed 100% when the two parts have opposite signs. (DC Pickup 2016/17, NA in production, is included here.)")
```

```{r agemix-sankeys}
                       "%: ", method_label)

  for (vc in classes) {
    for (y in 2014:2024) {
      df <- agemix |>
        filter(VehicleClass == vc, year == y) |>
        select(STNAME = statename, flow = count_agemix, rate)

                       sankey_title(vc, paste("yearpair", yp_label(y)), agemix_basis),
                       extra_note = spike_note(vc, y))
      save_sankey(s, sankey_stem(vc, yp_label(y), "agemix"))
    }
    for (ys in c("yrs_all", "yrs_excl")) {
      df <- agemix_win |>
        filter(year_set == ys, VehicleClass == vc) |>
        select(STNAME = statename, flow, rate)
      s <- make_sankey(df,
                       sankey_title(vc, paste("averaged over", year_set_labels[ys]), agemix_basis),
                       extra_note = "Tennessee 2014/15 dropped as in production, so this window is not exactly balanced.")
      save_sankey(s, sankey_stem(vc, paste0("avg_", ys), "agemix"))
    }
  }
}
```

# 5. Conclusions

```{r conclusion-numbers}
n_verdict <- function(vc, v) sum(stability$VehicleClass == vc & stability$verdict_group == v)
states_with <- function(v, vc = classes) {
  stability |>
    filter(verdict_group == v, VehicleClass %in% vc) |>
    summarise(classes = str_flatten(VehicleClass, "/"), .by = statename) |>
    mutate(txt = paste0(statename, " (", classes, ")")) |>
    pull(txt) |>
    str_flatten_comma(", and ")
}
bal_rng <- balance_year |>
  summarise(lo = min(imports_pct_of_exports), hi = max(imports_pct_of_exports), .by = VehicleClass)
win_bal <- balance_win |> filter(year_set == "yrs_excl")
gross_ratio <- balance_year |>
  summarise(mean_year = mean(gross_exports), .by = VehicleClass) |>
  left_join(filter(balance_win, year_set == "yrs_all") |> select(VehicleClass, avg = gross_exports),
            by = join_by(VehicleClass)) |>
  mutate(ratio = avg / mean_year)
sign_flipped <- stability |>
  filter(flag_spike, sign(avg_all) != sign(avg_no_spikes)) |>
  summarise(classes = str_flatten(VehicleClass, "/"), .by = statename) |>
  mutate(txt = paste0(statename, " (", classes, ")")) |>
  pull(txt) |>
  str_flatten_comma(", and ")
ov15   <- overlap |> filter(k == 15, reference == "yrs_excl average")
ov5    <- overlap |> filter(k == 5, reference == "yrs_excl average")
ov15_p <- overlap |> filter(k == 15, reference == "previous yearpair")
```

**Stability.** Most states' averages hold up. Of the 51 states, `r n_verdict("Car", "Stable")` (Car), `r n_verdict("SUV", "Stable")` (SUV) and `r n_verdict("Pickup", "Stable")` (Pickup) keep the same importer/exporter role in at least 80% of yearpairs with no material spike or trend. State rankings are persistent: persistent between-state differences account for `r pct(min(var_share$between_share[var_share$sample == "spikes removed"]))`–`r pct(max(var_share$between_share[var_share$sample == "spikes removed"]))` of the state-yearpair variance once spikes are removed, and adjacent yearpairs' rankings correlate at ρ ≈ `r round(median(rank_cor[["vs previous yearpair"]], na.rm = TRUE), 2)` (median).

The averages that are *not* stable fall into three groups:

- **Spike-driven averages:** `r states_with("Spike-driven average")`. One or two yearpairs with registration-data jumps (+15% to +28% of the state's stock in a single year in 2022/23, usually in all three classes at once) move the all-years average by at least 0.5 pp. For `r sign_flipped` the spike flips the sign of the all-years average, so the `yrs_all` Sankey puts them on the wrong side. `yrs_excl` drops the 2022/23 spikes, but the 2016/17 (Michigan Car, DC SUV) and 2024/25 (Oklahoma Car −19%, Rhode Island Car and SUV −11% to −14%) spikes are still inside it.
- **Trending:** `r states_with("Trending")`. The rate drifts by ≥ 1 pp over the decade (BH-adjusted q < 0.05), so the average depends on the window.
- **Role flips:** `r states_with("Role flips")`. These are mostly near-zero states (|average| ≲ 1.3%) whose sign switches from year to year; their Sankey side (importer vs exporter) in any averaged diagram is not meaningful. Oklahoma is different: its Car and SUV rates step down from around −1% before 2020/21 to −7% to −10% (Car, then −19% in 2024/25) and −3% to −11% (SUV) from 2021/22 on. That is a level shift, which looks more like a data or coverage change than a gradual trend.

**Per-yearpair Sankeys vs averages.** The top of each Sankey is steady: the median yearpair shares `r median(ov15$exporters)` of 15 top exporters and `r median(ov15$importers)` of 15 top importers with the `yrs_excl` averaged Sankey (top 5: `r median(ov5$exporters)` and `r median(ov5$importers)` of 5), and `r median(ov15_p$exporters)` / `r median(ov15_p$importers)` of 15 with the previous yearpair. The lower ranks churn, and two things reshuffle the top. First, spike yearpairs: in 2022/23 Virginia, Missouri and Maryland become the three largest Car and SUV importers. Second, large-stock states near zero: Texas Car is a top-3 exporter in 2015/16 and 2016/17 and the #1 importer in four other yearpairs, yet only a minor importer in the averages. Gross movement is larger in any single yearpair than in the averaged Sankeys: the `yrs_all` averaged Car Sankey shows `r pct(gross_ratio$ratio[gross_ratio$VehicleClass == "Car"])` of the mean per-yearpair gross exports (SUV `r pct(gross_ratio$ratio[gross_ratio$VehicleClass == "SUV"])`, Pickup `r pct(gross_ratio$ratio[gross_ratio$VehicleClass == "Pickup"])`), because averaging counts cancels sign switches.

**Balance.** Per yearpair, gross imports run `r pct(bal_rng$lo[bal_rng$VehicleClass == "Car"])`–`r pct(bal_rng$hi[bal_rng$VehicleClass == "Car"])` of gross exports for Car, `r pct(bal_rng$lo[bal_rng$VehicleClass == "SUV"])`–`r pct(bal_rng$hi[bal_rng$VehicleClass == "SUV"])` for SUV and `r pct(bal_rng$lo[bal_rng$VehicleClass == "Pickup"])`–`r pct(bal_rng$hi[bal_rng$VehicleClass == "Pickup"])` for Pickup (the `yrs_excl` averaged Sankeys: Car `r pct(win_bal$imports_pct_of_exports[win_bal$VehicleClass == "Car"], 0.1)`, SUV `r pct(win_bal$imports_pct_of_exports[win_bal$VehicleClass == "SUV"], 0.1)`, Pickup `r pct(win_bal$imports_pct_of_exports[win_bal$VehicleClass == "Pickup"], 0.1)`). Using per-yearpair data does not close the gap; Car is worst in 2023/24 and 2024/25. The gap is not estimation noise: it is exactly the error from applying one synthetic national age mix to every state's actual fleet, mostly the difference between state and national age mixes, plus (for Car since 2020/21) the national car fleet ageing away from the synthetic weights. Counting survivors age by age against national survival (age-mix accounting) balances every yearpair to exactly 100% without any rescaling, while changing state rates very little (R² ≥ `r round(min(agemix_fit$r2), 3)`; mean absolute change `r round(100 * min(agemix_fit$mean_abs_diff), 2)`–`r round(100 * max(agemix_fit$mean_abs_diff), 2)` pp). Since 2026-10-14 the production Sankeys in `survival.qmd` use these age-mix counts for vehicle numbers and ribbon widths, keeping the national-survival-weighted rate for their % labels.
